name: Flight school

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)
A.staff: Owen and Mia (instructors at the school's airport)

services.name: 2-hour dual lesson
services.story: The main story: a 2-hour dual lesson in the 4-seat trainer, $470 for the block. A card is saved for the $75 fee; the block is charged at DONE.

services.name: 1-hour ground lesson
services.story: A 1-hour ground lesson, $90. A card is saved for the $75 fee, and Alex pays at the front desk after.

services.name: discovery flight
services.story: A $149 discovery flight, paid in full when booking.

services.name: ground school course (10 evenings)
services.story: The $399 private pilot ground school course: a $100 deposit now, and the $299 rest paid at the front desk at the first evening.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer
B.staff: Ravi and Ines (instructors who fly to the customer's airport)
B.customer: Alex M. (pilot, owner of the aircraft) · other customers

services.name: flight review in your own aircraft
services.story: The main story: a 3-hour flight review in Alex's own aircraft at Alex's home airport, $255. The saved card is charged at DONE.

services.name: ground school seat
services.story: A $45 seat at a ground school class at a host's place, paid in full.

services.name: transition training (estimate)
services.story: Transition training in a newly bought aircraft: a $300 deposit on the $1,200 estimate, and the $900 rest on the bill after the last visit.

services_shape: a person's time (an instructor) plus an aircraft or the simulator for lessons; an aircraft or the simulator alone for a student's supervised solo, with an instructor on duty; seats on a timetable for the ground school course; flow B: an instructor at the customer's own aircraft and airport, and a ground school class at a host's place
questions_before_times: new to flying, a student pilot, or a licensed pilot (sets the service: a discovery flight, the next lesson, a solo, a flight review or checkout)
what the lesson is for, and the next stage of training if the student knows it
which aircraft type, if the pilot is checked out in one
for a discovery flight: how many people fly, and whether a guest under 18 is coming
for a flight in the customer's own aircraft (flow B): the airport and the aircraft type
safety_stop: an aircraft crash or fire happening now, someone hurt at the airport, an aircraft overdue or missing
first_steps: Proof of citizenship, or the federal security approval
license: none checked by Rosie: a flight school needs no state license in most places; where the state licenses flight schools as private or vocational schools, the business says so (a switch from the state form). Each instructor's federal flight instructor certificate is the business's own word
staff_skills: discovery flights, primary training, instrument, multi-engine, tailwheel, checkout flights, flight reviews, simulator, ground school, stage checks (the chief instructor or a second instructor)
messages_never: weight, date of birth, medical certificate details, health answers, citizenship papers and certificate numbers never go in a text: only the secure page
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
